  "body": "The account is careful in the right places — a1's hedge on bad faith is honest, a7 catches a real internal limitation, and the calm meta-conversation separated from incidents survives everything I say below. But I have grounds for five objections.

First, the diagnosis is innocent memory failure, and the remedy has no answer if the vagueness is motivated. a1 concedes bad faith is not excluded, then the whole remedy stack proceeds as if innocence held. If one flatmate benefits from interpretive slack — agrees loosely, then retroactively narrows what they promised — a written trial threatens them, and they will resist or game it: dispute the criteria, neglect to record, litigate the record itself. The account's only failure contingency (a8) is the avoiding friend's refusal, and its escape hatch — questioning the living arrangement — is nuclear. The missing case is the cheerful attender who quietly defeats the mechanism.

Second, a5's 'written input counts as full participation' conflates participation in the conversation with contribution to the household. Under a disengagement reading of the avoidance — which a3's hedge permits but the remedy ignores — the asynchronous channel hands the avoider a certified way to offer occasional text and nothing else. The account treats refusal of the channel as diagnostic; acceptance is equally diagnostic, and the account never reads it. The channel's value depends on pairing input with observable chore outcomes, which a5 does not require.

Third, the strategy family is 'coordinate better'; 'coordinate less' is never considered. Domain ownership (your own dishes, your own rooms, a short shared list) or buying out the conflict with a cleaner shrinks the coordination surface instead of managing it, and by the account's own a2 — churn is what silently kills fixed deals — decoupled arrangements degrade gracefully where weekly resets degrade badly. The stack (trial, records, resets, meta-conversation, channel) also bureaucratizes a friendship; whether that cost is worth paying depends on stakes the material doesn't show, and the account never poses the proportionality question.

Fourth, the trial inherits the disease it cures. No success criterion for the two weeks is pre-agreed. A household that cannot agree afterward what 'clean the kitchen' meant will not agree afterward whether the trial went well; day fourteen becomes the next meaning-dispute, one level up. This is fixable — record the verdict test alongside the trial — but under a2's churn 'were things better' is genuinely contestable, so the fix is substantive, not clerical.

Fifth, done-criteria presuppose the standards agreement that may be the actual fight. 'Counters wiped' is a criterion only once the household agrees what wiped looks like. If some disputes are about standards rather than recollection, drafting criteria relocates the argument to drafting time. Arguably that surfaces the real disagreement, which is a1's own logic — but then fewer disputes will be 'checkable against a record' than a4's consequence promises.

Two caveats on my own grounds: the motivated-vagueness reading in the first objection is as speculative as the memory reading it challenges — I cannot distinguish them from this material either; the robust complaint is that the remedy assumes one of them. And the proportionality worry depends on goodwill and stakes I cannot see. One bookkeeping note: the weekly reset, substantive in the body, has no commitments record, so its reliance on a2 is unexpressed.",

Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# objection

Develop criticism of the account where you have grounds. It is possible that your objection, its relevance, or the problem formulation is mistaken.

## Original problem (task)
[01274f41553299e7] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input account (p.objection.0)
[4c180fd4e335e52b] (h005.fork5.p.objection.0)
Source account: daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account; selected view: both
Artifact: 671b1206f339e133c75cc719c48aa19bacf4c6b9728c3f45b4fc66cef940f3fa

Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
This is a first account, so I am working only from the task as stated, which is thin in places and forces conjecture that I will flag as such.

Three features of the situation seem to do most of the explanatory work, and they reinforce one another. First, the pattern of agreeing and then disagreeing about what the agreement meant. Read neutrally, that is not a dishonesty problem; it is what informal, spoken, in-passing household agreements reliably produce. Each person hears the version that fits their assumptions, carries away a different memory, and discovers the divergence only when a chore goes undone. My conjecture: most of this class of argument disappears once agreements are recorded where everyone can see them, with an explicit criterion for what counts as done — not “clean the kitchen” but “dishes washed, counters wiped, bin out by Sunday night.”

Second, the changing work schedules. Any fixed chore allocation has a silent expiry date. A split that was reasonable when one friend had free mornings stops being fair the week their shifts change, but nobody announces the expiry — so it surfaces as “you didn’t do your chore,” when the truer statement is “the deal no longer matches the week.” This suggests the arrangement should be rebuilt for churn: a brief weekly reset, or assignment keyed to who is actually home, rather than a permanent rota.

Third, the friend who has started avoiding the conversations. Avoidance is information: the conversations have become costly. If talking about chores predictably turns into an argument, skipping the talk is a rational response, and pressing that friend to attend more of the same meetings will likely deepen the withdrawal. The better move is to change the format, not to enlarge the attendance requirement — a shared note they can edit on their own time counts as participation.

So my sequenced suggestion: (1) raise the pattern, not the latest incident, at a calm scheduled moment rather than mid-dispute; (2) offer a short trial — say two weeks — of written, specific, done-criteria agreements kept somewhere shared; (3) build in a weekly ten-minute reset, or its asynchronous equivalent, to absorb schedule changes; (4) hand the avoiding friend the low-friction channel and treat their edits as full participation; (5) keep friendship-talk and chore-negotiation-talk distinguishable, since the friendships are the asset that matters most here.

One caution: clarity is not the same as fairness. Once tasks are visible, someone may discover the split was actually lopsided all along, and the asker should be ready to renegotiate the division itself, not just its wording. And two things the material does not tell me: whether the disputes track real inequity or only mismatched recollections, and how much goodwill remains. If the avoiding friend also refuses the asynchronous channel, the problem has changed shape — from how to manage chores to whether this living arrangement is still workable — and that harder question is not answered by anything here.
COMMITMENTS

This is a conjecture, not an observed fact about that friend.","scope":"Interpretation of the avoiding friend"},{"id":"a4","type":"commitment","text":"Propose a short, explicit trial (e.g., two weeks) in which each chore agreement is recorded in a shared place with a named person, a done-criterion, and a time.","action":"Initiate a time-boxed written-agreement trial","consequence":"Disputes about meaning become checkable against a record rather than contested from memory.","depends":["a1","a2"]},{"id":"a5","type":"commitment","text":"Offer the avoiding friend an asynchronous, low-stakes channel — e.g., the shared note editable on their own time — and count their written input as full participation instead of requiring meeting attendance.","action":"Open an asynchronous input channel","depends":["a3"]},{"id":"a6","type":"commitment","text":"Raise the recurring pattern at a calm, scheduled moment rather than during an active dispute, and keep the friendship conversation separate from the chore-negotiation conversation.","action":"Hold one calm meta-conversation separated from incidents"},{"id":"a7","type":"objection","text":"Clarity alone may not resolve the disputes: once tasks are recorded, a genuine imbalance of effort may become visible, and the asker should be prepared to renegotiate the split itself, not merely its wording.","target":["a4"],"bearing":"Limits the claimed sufficiency of the written-agreement trial."},{"id":"a8","type":"problem","text":"Unresolved from the material: whether the arguments track real inequity or only divergent recollections; whether the avoiding friend also avoids doing chores; and what follows if even asynchronous coordination is refused — at which point the question shifts from chore management to the viability of the living arrangement."}],"uptake":["a4","a5","a6","a7"]}
